# Pivot Letter Template — Clinical (nursing or allied health) to Nonclinical

```
[FIRST NAME, LAST-INITIAL]
[ONE CONTACT — email]

Dear [NAME, else "Hiring Team"],

[HOOK — the two worlds meet: one sentence naming the role AND your
clinical specificity. Skeleton: "You're hiring a [ROLE] for
[WHAT THE CUSTOMER/END USER DOES ALL DAY], and I've spent [N] years
being exactly that end user."]

[TRANSLATION PARAGRAPH — 3–4 sentences, proof-bank facts said in
nonclinical language:
  quality huddles / dashboards you built / tech rollouts you piloted /
  checklists that stuck / people you trained / operations you ran.
  At least one number or concrete artifact. No clinical jargon.

[GAP + BRIDGE — one honest sentence about what you don't have
("SaaS account management, certifications, a classroom in X"),
one bridge sentence ("what I have instead is ..."). Stop there.
One bridge, once.]

[CLOSE + HOOK-BACK — one sentence offering something concrete:
"I'd welcome the chance to talk about where the pain actually
lives on the floor." Then "Thank you for reading."]

[FIRST NAME, LAST-INITIAL]
```

## Jargon scrub before sending

Cross out: SBAR, q-shift, POC, the unit's internal codes, any
department shorthand. Say "shift report," "point of care," or
plain English. Chapter 4 has the full translation table.
